subject: Appeal: regional filtered outage — request for uptime apportionment and credit
messages:
From: Ian Brooks <ian.brooks@brightleafhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@brightleafhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: Impact on BrightLeaf API — request for credit apportionment

Logan,

We saw a sharp increase in 502/504s across our EU-PROD and US-WEST clusters starting ~2027-05-14T15:10Z and lasting in degraded form until ~2027-05-14T17:50Z. Your status page shows a "regional routing anomaly" and points to EdgeFlux as the upstream. Our telemetry (attached) indicates request success dropped from 99.984% to ~98.2% for that 2.6 hour window, but critically the degradation was path-dependent: only a subset of our edge POPs saw full outage while others had high latency.

Our contract (SLA §3.2) entitles BrightLeaf to a pro-rata credit for service availability shortfalls except when a maintenance window is declared by Redwood or a third-party maintenance explicitly excluded in the SLA applies. Redwood's incident post says the event was a third-party outage, but EdgeFlux's summary (we were forwarded a copy) lists a failover cascade that partially impacted only one backbone region and did not qualify as scheduled maintenance.

We request a review of uptime apportionment for this event and a credit consistent with the partial-degradation accounting in §5.1. We have attached logs, short trace snippets, and the EdgeFlux PDF. Please advise next steps and an expected timeline for resolution.

Thanks,
Ian Brooks
Head of Platform Engineering
BrightLeaf Health

Attachments: brightleaf_service_logs_20270514.zip, edgeflux-incident-summary.pdf

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Ian Brooks <ian.brooks@brightleafhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 20:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Impact on BrightLeaf API — request for credit apportionment

Ian — thanks for the detailed packet, and sorry for the disruption. I’ve looped in Marissa (SLA ops) and Monica (customer reliability) to help with apportionment review and to validate whether the EdgeFlux event fits the SLA exclusion criteria.

Quick notes up front:
- We’re treating this as an escalation; I will get you a preliminary calculation within 48 hours and a final position within 7 business days.
- Two separate technical questions we’ll answer in the packet: (1) was the impact attributable to EdgeFlux exclusively, and (2) even if a third-party caused the trigger, whether the partial-degradation rules (prefix/KV caching overlap and path-level failover) imply we owe a pro-rata credit.

Next steps on our side: Marissa will run the uptime ledger using our path-aware apportionment algorithm (we posted it to the internal ticket linked below) and Monica will coordinate with the EdgeFlux ops team for their incident timeline.

Logan
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

On-call/Contact: +1 (415) 555-0122
Related ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9821

From: Sara Li <sara.li@brightleafhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Impact on BrightLeaf API — request for credit apportionment

Hi Logan/Marissa — adding a couple of clarifying points from our end:
- The affected flows were primarily our med-ingest endpoints that route through the us-west-pop-4 and eu-central-pop-2 prefixes. Traffic that routed via us-west-pop-2 and eu-central-pop-1 saw nominal latency.
- We have a short runbook excerpt showing automated retry behavior that amplified downstream errors for some clients; we included that in the logs.
- BrightLeaf's security/compliance team will need the final apportionment and the raw EdgeFlux timeline to complete our audit.

Please keep us posted.

—Sara
Senior SRE, BrightLeaf Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: proposed apportionment and note to legal

Team — summary after preliminary ledger run:
- Total incident window observed in our probes: 2027-05-14T15:07Z -> 2027-05-14T17:52Z (2h45m).
- Measured customer-facing error-rate delta (BrightLeaf-specific routing pattern): equivalent availability drop of 1.78 percentage points across their weighted request mix.
- Our path-aware apportionment model indicates ~61% of the impact aligns to EdgeFlux backbone failure, while ~39% looks attributable to Redwood failover/async cache-stalling behavior. Rationale: KV cache stampede and additional tokenization penalty when requests were routed to cold nodes.

Recommendation: offer a pro-rata credit equal to the portion attributable to Redwood (39% of the outage window) per SLA §5.1, plus expedited mitigation tasks to address cache warmup during cross-pop failover. This preserves the third-party exclusion stance where appropriate but recognizes our contribution to customer pain.

Action items:
- Approve credit letter draft to BrightLeaf (I’ll draft and share).
- Monica to request formal timeline from EdgeFlux (I’ll include the PL to legal for the possibility that EdgeFlux’s contract limits do not fully exclude credits).
- If legal or sales wants to negotiate a goodwill adjustment beyond the calculated share, we can escalate to Logan for sign-off.

I’ll attach the ledger CSV and the calculation workbook to internal ticket INF-9821.

—Marissa
SLA Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
